spec.description: Open pull requests, open issues and code scanning alerts across your GitHub repositories, and the Actions runs that failed recently. Every row links to GitHub, and a bar chart shows which repositories fail most.

spec.title: Open PRs
spec.description: Pull requests open across your repositories, from the most recent scan. Renovate pull requests are left out. The tile turns yellow at 5 and red at 15, and the table below lists each one with a link. Trust a 0 only while Scout status reads Running.

spec.expr: sum(max_over_time({container="github-scout"} |= `scan complete` | json msg="msg", open_prs="open_prs" | msg=`scan complete` | unwrap open_prs [$window]))

spec.title: Open issues
spec.description: Issues open across your repositories, from the most recent scan. Renovate and automated tracker issues are left out. The tile turns yellow at 5 and red at 20, and the table below lists each one with a link.

spec.expr: sum(max_over_time({container="github-scout"} |= `scan complete` | json msg="msg", open_issues="open_issues" | msg=`scan complete` | unwrap open_issues [$window]))

spec.title: Code scanning alerts
spec.description: Open code scanning alerts across your repositories, from the most recent scan. The tile turns yellow at 1 and red at 5, and the table below has each alert's severity and a link. It keeps the highest count of the last 30 minutes by default, so one failed scan cannot hide alerts. Trust a 0 only while Scan integrity reads OK.

spec.expr: sum(max_over_time({container="github-scout"} |= `scan complete` | json msg="msg", code_alerts="code_alerts" | msg=`scan complete` | unwrap code_alerts [$window]))

spec.title: Failed CI runs in this range
spec.description: Actions runs that failed, timed out or did not start, reported in the selected time range, each run counted once. Unlike the other tiles, this one follows the time picker. Any failure means CI broke somewhere, so the tile turns orange at 1 and red at 10. After a restart github-scout reports the last `LOOKBACK_HOURS` again, so a range can include a run that started before it.

spec.expr: count(count by (run_id) (count_over_time({container="github-scout"} |= `workflow run` | json | msg=`workflow run` | conclusion=~`failure|timed_out|startup_failure` [$__range])))

spec.title: Open pull requests
spec.description: Every open pull request from the most recent scan, newest first. Renovate pull requests are left out. Sort by any column from its header, and open a pull request on GitHub from the Link column.

spec.expr: count by (repo, number, title, author, draft, url, created_at) (count_over_time({container="github-scout"} | json | msg=`open pull request` [$window]))

spec.title: Open issues
spec.description: Every open issue from the most recent scan, newest first. Renovate and automated tracker issues are left out. Open an issue on GitHub from the Link column.

spec.expr: count by (repo, number, title, author, labels, url, created_at) (count_over_time({container="github-scout"} | json | msg=`open issue` [$window]))

spec.title: Code scanning alerts
spec.description: Every open code scanning alert from the most recent scan, newest first, with GitHub's severity. Repositories without code scanning are left out, and so are forks by default, because a fork reports the alerts of the code it copied as its own. To leave out another repository, list it in `CODE_SCANNING_EXCLUDE_REPOS`. If the table shows an error instead of rows, raise `max_query_series` in your Loki limits.

spec.expr: count by (repo, number, rule, severity, tool, url, created_at) (count_over_time({container="github-scout"} | json | msg=`code scanning alert` [$window]))

spec.title: Failed runs
spec.description: Failed, timed-out and never-started Actions runs reported in the selected time range, newest first, each run listed once. After a restart github-scout reports the last `LOOKBACK_HOURS` again, 72 hours by default, so a range can include a run that started before it. Keep the time picker within `LOOKBACK_HOURS`. If the table shows an error instead of rows, narrow the time range or raise `max_query_series` in your Loki limits.

spec.expr: count by (repo, workflow, conclusion, branch, event, run_number, run_id, url, created_at) (count_over_time({container="github-scout"} |= `workflow run` | json | msg=`workflow run` | conclusion=~`failure|timed_out|startup_failure` [$__range]))

spec.title: Scout status
spec.description: Shows whether github-scout finished a scan in the last hour. It scans every 15 minutes by default. Stalled means the scanner is stuck or the container is down, and every panel above goes stale. Scan integrity beside it shows whether the scans could read everything.

spec.title: Scan integrity
spec.description: Shows whether github-scout logged an error in the last 30 minutes by default. Degraded means a scan could not run or could not read a signal, for example because the token was revoked, GitHub rate-limited it or the network timed out. The container logs have the detail. Routine warnings, such as code scanning being unavailable on a repository, do not count.

spec.title: Failures by repository
spec.description: Failed, timed-out and never-started Actions runs per repository, reported in the selected time range, each run counted once. Every bar is red from 1 failed run, and a repository with many is worth a look for a flaky or broken workflow. After a restart github-scout reports the last `LOOKBACK_HOURS` again, so a range can include a run that started before it. An empty panel means CI was green everywhere.

spec.expr: count by (repo) (count by (repo, run_id) (count_over_time({container="github-scout"} |= `workflow run` | json msg="msg", repo="repo", run_id="run_id", conclusion="conclusion" | msg=`workflow run` | conclusion=~`failure|timed_out|startup_failure` [$__range])))

defaults.noValue: No failed runs in this range

spec.title: GitHub Scout

spec.name: window
spec.label: Snapshot window
spec.description: How far back to look for the latest scan of open pull requests, issues and alerts. Keep it at least as long as `SCAN_INTERVAL`. The default 30m is twice the default scan interval, so one slow scan does not empty the tables. The time picker changes only the failed-run panels.
